To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the new series of platinum(II) complexes containing cyclopentyl-amine as a primary ligand and bidentate leaving group, are active in vitro on KB tumour cell line and in vivo against P388, L121O, ADJ/ PC6A and Yoshide sarcoma.
the Pt(cpa) 2 (5-sulfophthalate) was the best compound against P388, L121O, ADJ/pc6A and Yoshidasarcoma.
a new series of platinum(II) complexes with bidentate ligands, containing primary amines and phthalic or isophthalic acid derivatives, have been synthesized and characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis and antitumourogenic activity of a new series (Pt(cpa)2L2) of Pt (II)-amine complexes, where cyclopentyl-amine is used as a primary amine ligand, and L represents a bidentate leaving group, such as nitro-, dintro- or sulfo-phthalic and isophtalic anions.
the synthesis and biological evaluation of Pt (II)-amine complexes with leaving groups which are not directly bound to the metal atom.
the search of a new class of Pt (II)-complexes with antitumour effect, which is not yet fully exploited.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Pt (II) compounds with cyclopentane derivatives are a good starting point for the synthesis of new potential antitumour drugs, but the results obtained so far do not allow us to make any definite predictions.
Pt (cpa)2(5-sulfo-isophtalato) was the most active compound, followed by Pt (cpa)(NO2-IPA)(5-sulfoIPA), Pt (cpa), (NO2-phth)2 and Pt (cpa). (2NO2-IPA)2.
Pt(II) complexes of cyclopentyl amine are promising antitumor agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the complexes containing the 1- and 2-nitro-derivatives of the phthalic anion, as well as those containing 1-nitro-derivative of the isophthalic acid anion, are more effective than the complexes containing the corresponding sulfo-derivates.

the antitumour effect of Pt (II)-amine complexes is strongly influenced by the nature of the leaving ligands, and that the complexes with the sulfo-derivates of isophthalic acid are more active than the corresponding phthalic acid complexes.
the antitumour Pt (II) complex with cyclopentylethanolamine and 5-sulfo-isophthalic acid is a promising new compound with a good therapeutic index.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antitumor effect of these complexes depends on the nature of leaving groups, and the cyclopentyl ligand is a good candidate for the synthesis of new Pt (II)-based antitumor agents.
a good cytostatics and antitumours activity can be achieved in the series of Pt (ii) complexes with cyclo-pentylamine as a primary amine ligand.
the new complexes are active against experimental tumours in vivo, and that the antitumour effects of Pt(II) compounds can be modulated by changing the leaving ligands.
